questions.question: What should you do with a disruptive passenger?

options.text: Remove them from the bus immediately, no matter where you are.
Let them off at the next bus stop.
Keep them on the bus and drive to the police department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them off at the next bus stop.
questions.explanation: Even if a passenger is disruptive, you must keep them safe. Let them off at the next scheduled stop or at a safe place with other people around.

questions.question: What should you do if your engine catches fire?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine as soon as possible to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless you have to.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what might happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything about railroad crossings.
The examiner might ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner might ask you to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a real railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a pretend location.

questions.question: What affects your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) the most?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol you drink
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends mainly on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when going downhill?
questions.correctAnswerText: It speeds up.
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle downhill and makes it go faster.

questions.question: How does a posted speed limit for cars apply to buses?

options.text: It is usually safe for buses too.
It may be too fast for buses.
It may be too slow for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be too fast for buses.
questions.explanation: Speed limits for cars may not be safe for buses, especially on curves. Be extra careful when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: What does fresh oil under your vehicle mean before a trip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong.
questions.explanation: Fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks under your vehicle are warning signs. Check these before you drive.

questions.question: How can you avoid a hazard on the road?

options.text: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder can help you avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough for large vehicles.

questions.question: Is it safe to eat while driving?

options.text: Yes, if the food is easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is dangerous.
questions.explanation: Eating, smoking, or drinking while driving take your attention off the road. Plan your trips so you can stop to eat.

questions.question: What should you do if you hear or feel something unusual while driving?

options.text: Hope the vehicle will be okay until another driver takes over.
Stop and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, have it checked right away.

questions.question: How can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when you start to move?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before you take your foot off the brake.
Place the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before you take your foot off the brake.
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before you remove your foot from the brake pedal. This keeps your vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving.

questions.question: Drivers stuck behind a slow-moving vehicle often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Many drivers tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass safely.

questions.question: Before a bus enters a curve, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Buses should enter curves at slower speeds. Drivers should be extra careful if the road is wet or slippery.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Okay if the weather is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed.
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile phone while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: The heavier the vehicle:

options.text: The less important the brakes are.
The harder the brakes must work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes must work.
questions.explanation: Heavier vehicles need brakes to work harder to stop the vehicle.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good idea on long trips.
Takes your attention away from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous. It distracts you from the road and requires you to take a hand off the wheel.

questions.question: Front tires must have a tread depth of at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Front tires must have 4/32 of an inch tread depth. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, what is the minimum safe following distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Six seconds.
questions.explanation: At speeds under 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light might be:

options.text: A driver who doesn't know traffic rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: An impaired driver.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are on drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One sign is stopping at inappropriate places, like green lights.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is aware of what is happening around them.
May not be aware of what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around joggers, pedestrians, and cyclists wearing headphones. They cannot hear your vehicle and may do something dangerous without knowing you are there.
